name: Low-temperature hysteresis and SIRM cycling (300-5-300 K, 2.5 T) of submicron and mm magnetite across the Verwey transition
plain_name: Track how magnetite's stored magnetism changes when it is cooled through its 120 K transition
description: Submicron (0.037-0.22 um) magnetite dispersions and a 1.3 mm crystal: hysteresis loops to 1.5 T from about 15 K to 295 K (AGFM with liquid-He cryostat) and saturation isothermal remanence given in 2.5 T at 300 K, zero-field cooled to 5 K and warmed back to 300 K in an MPMS-2 SQUID magnetometer, to follow coercivity and domain-state changes at the Verwey transition (about 120 K).
keywords: Track how magnetite's stored magnetism changes when it is cooled through its 120 K transition

sources.citation: Ozdemir O., Dunlop D. J., Moskowitz B. M. Changes in remanence, coercivity and domain state at low temperature in magnetite. Earth Planet. Sci. Lett. 194 (2002) 343-358

reported_equipment: Princeton Measurements Corporation AGFM (MicroMag Model 2900) with a liquid He cryostat

requirements.rationale: Remanence cycling runs from 300 K to 5 K and back.
The SIRM is imparted in a 2.5 T field (the hysteresis loops need 1.5 T).
Optional: the hysteresis loops were taken in a liquid-helium cryostat.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
